result.rationale: The migration inserts raw site_setting values verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), bypassing the model's before_validation normalization (which strips `http(s)://` and paths). Meanwhile `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` uses `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host).first` exact-match, so a legacy entry like 'http://discourse.org' stored with the protocol would never match referer hosts after upgrade. The spec fixtures confirm hosts were stored with protocols ('http://discourse.org\nhttps://example.com/1234'). This is a real migration data-normalization defect int

judged_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P1, confidence 100, defect] `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` Migrating a legacy allowed-host entry containing `http://`, `https://`, or a path inserts it without model normalization, so the exact hostname lookup rejects that configured host after upgrade and all of its embeds stop loading until an admin resaves it.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug. Looking at the migration code, when migrating legacy hosts from site_settings, the code does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` where `h` comes directly from the old setting value. However, the EmbeddableHost model has a `before_validation` callback that normalizes hosts by stripping `http://`, `https://`, and paths. The migration bypasses this normalization by using raw SQL INSERT. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` where `host` is extracted from a URI (just the hostname). If the migrated data contains `http://example.com`, it won't match a lookup for `example.com`. This is a real data migration bug that would cause embeds to stop working after upgrade.
